## Visualize MRI Modalities

```{r viz_mri, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
tp1 <- test_patient$timepoints[[1]]

plot_mri_slice <- function(volume, title, z = NULL) {
  vol <- as.array(volume)
  if (is.null(z)) z <- dim(vol)[3] %/% 2
  slice <- vol[, , z]
  df <- expand.grid(x = seq_len(nrow(slice)), y = seq_len(ncol(slice)))
  df$intensity <- as.vector(slice)
  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = intensity)) +
    geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c() +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14))
}

plots <- list()
for (mod in tp1$mri$available) {
  plots[[mod]] <- plot_mri_slice(tp1$mri$volumes[[mod]], toupper(mod))
}

# Segmentation overlay
if (!is.null(tp1$segmentation$mask)) {
  seg <- as.array(tp1$segmentation$mask)
  ref_vol <- as.array(tp1$mri$volumes[[tp1$mri$available[1]]])
  z <- dim(ref_vol)[3] %/% 2

  df <- expand.grid(x = seq_len(nrow(ref_vol[,,z])), y = seq_len(ncol(ref_vol[,,z])))
  df$mri <- as.vector(ref_vol[, , z])
  df$seg <- factor(as.vector(seg[, , z]))

  plots[["segmentation"]] <- ggplot(df) +
    geom_raster(aes(x, y, fill = mri)) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c() +
    geom_tile(data = df %>% filter(seg != "0"),
              aes(x, y), fill = "red", alpha = 0.4) +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(title = "Segmentation Overlay") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14))
}

wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 3)
ggsave(file.path(RESULTS_PATH, "figures", "mri_modalities.png"),
       width = 15, height = 10, dpi = 150)
```

# 2. Preprocessing

```{r preprocess_patients}
# Process first N patients (adjust as needed)
# Start with 10, increase to 91 once you've confirmed it works
N_PATIENTS <- 10
# 64³ for CPU (use 128³ if you have GPU/more RAM)
TARGET_SIZE <- c(64L, 64L, 64L)

selected_patients <- patients %>%
  filter(n_timepoints >= 3) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_timepoints)) %>%
  head(N_PATIENTS)

cat("Processing", nrow(selected_patients), "patients with 3+ timepoints\n")

all_preprocessed <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_patients))) {
  pid <- selected_patients$patient_id[i]
  ppath <- selected_patients$path[i]

  cat("\n[", i, "/", nrow(selected_patients), "]", pid, "\n")

  patient_data <- tryCatch(
    load_full_patient(ppath),
    error = function(e) { cat("  SKIP:", e$message, "\n"); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(patient_data)) next

  preprocessed <- tryCatch(
    preprocess_full_patient(patient_data, target_size = TARGET_SIZE,
                             output_dir = file.path(PROCESSED_PATH, "registered")),
    error = function(e) { cat("  PREPROCESS FAIL:", e$message, "\n"); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(preprocessed)) next

  all_preprocessed[[pid]] <- list(
    patient_data = patient_data,
    preprocessed = preprocessed
  )
}

cat("\nSuccessfully preprocessed:", length(all_preprocessed), "patients\n")
```


# 6. Progression Classification (Rule-Based)

```{r progression_classification}
all_trajectories <- list()
all_progressions <- list()

for (pid in names(all_regions_raw)) {
  regions_by_tp <- all_regions_raw[[pid]]
  if (length(regions_by_tp) < 2) next

  tp_names <- names(regions_by_tp)
  patient_data <- all_preprocessed[[pid]]$patient_data
  time_weeks <- sapply(patient_data$timepoints[tp_names], `[[`, "week_number")

  trajectories <- list()
  for (r in regions_by_tp[[1]]) {
    vols <- c()
    for (tp in tp_names) {
      tp_regions <- regions_by_tp[[tp]]
      matched <- Filter(function(x) x$region_type == r$region_type, tp_regions)
      vol <- if (length(matched) > 0) matched[[1]]$volume_cm3 else 0
      vols <- c(vols, vol)
    }
    traj <- analyze_region_trajectory(vols, time_weeks)
    trajectories[[r$region_id]] <- traj
  }

  events <- all_event_tables[[pid]]
  if (is.null(events)) events <- tibble(event_type = character(0))

  progression <- classify_patient_progression(trajectories, events)

  all_trajectories[[pid]] <- trajectories
  all_progressions[[pid]] <- progression

  generate_patient_report(pid, combined_regions %>% filter(patient_id == pid),
                           events, trajectories, progression)
}
```

# 8. Segmentation: Using Provided Masks + 3D U-Net Architecture Demo

We use the automated segmentations provided by LUMIERE (HD-GLIO-AUTO and
DeepBraTumIA) as our segmentation input. This is the correct approach because:

- LUMIERE provides expert-validated automated segmentations
- Our research contribution is the **longitudinal framework**, not segmentation
- Training a 3D U-Net from scratch requires GPU hardware

Below we demonstrate our 3D U-Net architecture (verifying it runs) and evaluate
the quality of the provided segmentations.

```{r unet_architecture_demo}
source("R/03_model_3d_unet.R")

# Instantiate the model to show it works
model <- unet_3d(in_channels = 4L, n_classes = 4L, base_filters = 16L)

# Count parameters
n_params <- sum(sapply(model$parameters, function(p) prod(p$shape)))
cat("3D U-Net Architecture:\n")
cat("  Input:  4-channel MRI (T1, T1c, T2, FLAIR)\n")
cat("  Output: 4-class segmentation mask\n")
cat("  Parameters:", format(n_params, big.mark = ","), "\n")
cat("  Encoder: 4 levels (16 → 32 → 64 → 128 filters)\n")
cat("  Bottleneck: 256 filters\n")
cat("  Decoder: 4 levels with skip connections\n")
cat("  Loss: Dice + Cross-Entropy (combined)\n\n")

# Forward pass test with small dummy input (proves architecture works on CPU)
dummy_input <- torch_randn(1, 4, 32, 32, 32)
with_no_grad({
  dummy_output <- model(dummy_input)
})
cat("Forward pass test (32³ input):\n")
cat("  Input shape: ", paste(dim(dummy_input), collapse = " x "), "\n")
cat("  Output shape:", paste(dim(dummy_output), collapse = " x "), "\n")
cat("  Architecture verified on CPU.\n")
```

## Segmentation Quality Analysis

```{r seg_quality}
# Compare HD-GLIO-AUTO vs DeepBraTumIA segmentations
seg_comparison <- list()

for (pid in names(all_preprocessed)[1:min(5, length(all_preprocessed))]) {
  patient_data <- all_preprocessed[[pid]]$patient_data
  for (tp_name in names(patient_data$timepoints)) {
    tp <- patient_data$timepoints[[tp_name]]
    wpath <- tp$path

    hdglio_path <- file.path(wpath, "HD-GLIO-AUTO-segmentation",
                              "registered", "segmentation.nii.gz")
    dbta_path <- file.path(wpath, "DeepBraTumIA-segmentation",
                            "atlas", "segmentation", "seg_mask.nii.gz")

    if (file.exists(hdglio_path) && file.exists(dbta_path)) {
      seg1 <- as.array(safe_read_nifti(hdglio_path))
      seg2 <- as.array(safe_read_nifti(dbta_path))

      if (!is.null(seg1) && !is.null(seg2) && all(dim(seg1) == dim(seg2))) {
        dice <- compute_dice(seg1 > 0, seg2 > 0)
        seg_comparison <- c(seg_comparison, list(tibble(
          patient_id = pid, timepoint = tp_name,
          hdglio_labels = paste(sort(unique(as.integer(seg1))), collapse = ","),
          dbta_labels = paste(sort(unique(as.integer(seg2))), collapse = ","),
          dice_agreement = dice,
          hdglio_volume_mm3 = sum(seg1 > 0),
          dbta_volume_mm3 = sum(seg2 > 0)
        )))
      }
    }
  }
}

if (length(seg_comparison) > 0) {
  seg_df <- bind_rows(seg_comparison)
  cat("Segmentation Method Agreement (HD-GLIO-AUTO vs DeepBraTumIA):\n")
  cat("  Samples compared:", nrow(seg_df), "\n")
  cat("  Mean Dice:", round(mean(seg_df$dice_agreement), 4), "\n")
  cat("  Std Dice: ", round(sd(seg_df$dice_agreement), 4), "\n\n")
  print(seg_df %>% select(patient_id, timepoint, dice_agreement) %>%
          knitr::kable(digits = 4))
}
```

> **Note**: The 3D U-Net architecture is fully implemented in `R/03_model_3d_unet.R`
> and can be trained on GPU hardware (Google Colab or cloud). For this analysis,
> we use the LUMIERE-provided segmentations as our primary segmentation input.

# 9. Train LSTM (Progression Model) — CPU-Friendly

The LSTM operates on tiny feature sequences (13 features x 20 timesteps),
not raw images. **This trains on CPU in under 5 minutes.**

```{r prepare_lstm_data}
source("R/08_model_lstm.R")

# Build feature sequences for each patient
# For now, use rule-based RANO-like labels as targets
# (Replace with actual RANO labels when CSV is available)

lstm_sequences <- list()
lstm_labels <- c()

for (pid in names(all_progressions)) {
  pt_regions <- combined_regions %>% filter(patient_id == pid)
  pt_events <- combined_events %>% filter(patient_id == pid)
  timepoints <- sort(unique(pt_regions$timepoint))

  if (length(timepoints) < 2) next

  MAX_SEQ <- 20L
  N_FEAT <- 13L
  seq_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = MAX_SEQ, ncol = N_FEAT)

  for (t_idx in seq_along(timepoints)) {
    if (t_idx > MAX_SEQ) break
    tp <- timepoints[t_idx]
    tp_data <- pt_regions %>% filter(timepoint == tp)

    total_vol <- sum(tp_data$volume_cm3, na.rm = TRUE)
    n_regions <- nrow(tp_data)
    max_vol <- max(tp_data$volume_cm3, na.rm = TRUE)
    mean_vol <- mean(tp_data$volume_cm3, na.rm = TRUE)

    vol_change <- 0; vol_pct <- 0; max_growth <- 0; max_disp <- 0
    n_grow <- 0; n_appear <- 0; n_disappear <- 0; n_split <- 0; n_merge <- 0

    if (t_idx > 1) {
      prev_tp <- timepoints[t_idx - 1]
      prev_vol <- pt_regions %>%
        filter(timepoint == prev_tp) %>%
        summarise(v = sum(volume_cm3, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
        pull(v)
      vol_change <- total_vol - prev_vol
      vol_pct <- if (prev_vol > 0) vol_change / prev_vol else 0

      tp_ev <- pt_events %>% filter(to_tp == tp)
      n_appear <- sum(tp_ev$event_type == "APPEARANCE")
      n_disappear <- sum(tp_ev$event_type == "DISAPPEARANCE")
      n_split <- sum(tp_ev$event_type == "SPLIT")
      n_merge <- sum(tp_ev$event_type == "MERGE")

      tp_lf <- long_features %>% filter(patient_id == pid, to_tp == tp)
      if (nrow(tp_lf) > 0) {
        max_growth <- max(tp_lf$pct_volume_change, na.rm = TRUE)
        max_disp <- max(tp_lf$centroid_displacement, na.rm = TRUE)
        n_grow <- sum(tp_lf$pct_volume_change > 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    }

    seq_mat[t_idx, ] <- c(total_vol, n_regions, max_vol, mean_vol,
                            vol_change, vol_pct, max_growth, max_disp,
                            n_grow, n_appear, n_disappear, n_split, n_merge)
  }

  lstm_sequences <- c(lstm_sequences, list(seq_mat))

  # Use our rule-based classification as training target
  prog <- all_progressions[[pid]]$classification
  label <- match(prog, c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD")) - 1L
  lstm_labels <- c(lstm_labels, label)
}

cat("LSTM sequences:", length(lstm_sequences), "\n")
cat("Label distribution:\n")
print(table(c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD")[lstm_labels + 1]))
```

```{r train_lstm}
if (length(lstm_sequences) >= 10) {
  set.seed(42)
  n <- length(lstm_sequences)
  train_idx <- sample(n, floor(n * 0.8))
  val_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(n), train_idx)

  cat("Train:", length(train_idx), "| Val:", length(val_idx), "\n")

  lstm_result <- train_lstm(
    train_sequences = lstm_sequences[train_idx],
    train_labels    = lstm_labels[train_idx],
    val_sequences   = lstm_sequences[val_idx],
    val_labels      = lstm_labels[val_idx],
    input_size  = 13L,
    hidden_size = 64L,
    num_layers  = 2L,
    n_classes   = 4L,
    epochs      = 80L,
    batch_size  = 8L,
    lr          = 1e-3,
    save_path   = file.path(MODELS_PATH, "lstm_progression.pt")
  )

  cat("LSTM training complete!\n")
} else {
  cat("Need at least 10 patients with 2+ timepoints.\n")
  cat("Increase N_PATIENTS in Section 2.\n")
}
```

```{r lstm_history, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}
if (exists("lstm_result")) {
  p1 <- tibble(
    epoch = seq_along(lstm_result$history$train_loss),
    Train = lstm_result$history$train_loss,
    Val   = lstm_result$history$val_loss
  ) %>%
    pivot_longer(-epoch, names_to = "Split", values_to = "Loss") %>%
    ggplot(aes(epoch, Loss, color = Split)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    labs(title = "Loss") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Train = "#2563eb", Val = "#dc2626")) +
    theme_minimal()

  p2 <- tibble(
    epoch = seq_along(lstm_result$history$train_acc),
    Train = lstm_result$history$train_acc * 100,
    Val   = lstm_result$history$val_acc * 100
  ) %>%
    pivot_longer(-epoch, names_to = "Split", values_to = "Accuracy") %>%
    ggplot(aes(epoch, Accuracy, color = Split)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    labs(title = "Accuracy (%)") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Train = "#2563eb", Val = "#dc2626")) +
    theme_minimal()

  p1 + p2
  ggsave(file.path(RESULTS_PATH, "figures", "lstm_training.png"),
         width = 12, height = 4, dpi = 150)
}
```

# 11. Key Finding: Hidden Regional Changes

```{r hidden_changes, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
if (nrow(patient_summaries) > 0) {
  insight <- patient_summaries %>%
    mutate(
      total_says = case_when(
        total_vol_pct_change > 0.25 ~ "Growing",
        total_vol_pct_change < -0.25 ~ "Shrinking",
        TRUE ~ "Stable"
      ),
      regions_say = case_when(
        n_growing_regions > 0 & n_shrinking_regions > 0 ~ "Mixed (Hidden!)",
        n_growing_regions > 0 ~ "Growing",
        n_shrinking_regions > 0 ~ "Shrinking",
        TRUE ~ "Stable"
      ),
      disagree = total_says != regions_say
    )

  n_hidden <- sum(insight$disagree)
  cat("Patients where total volume HIDES regional changes:", n_hidden, "\n")
  cat("This is", round(n_hidden / nrow(insight) * 100, 1),
      "% of patients analyzed\n")

  ggplot(insight, aes(total_says, fill = regions_say)) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
    labs(title = "Total Volume vs Region-Wise Assessment",
         subtitle = paste(n_hidden, "patients show hidden regional changes"),
         x = "What Total Volume Says", y = "Patients",
         fill = "What Region-Wise\nAnalysis Reveals") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 13))

  ggsave(file.path(RESULTS_PATH, "figures", "hidden_changes.png"),
         width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)
}
```

# Summary

This notebook runs the **complete pipeline on CPU** (no GPU required):

1. Loaded LUMIERE dataset (91 patients, 638 timepoints)
2. Preprocessed MRI (normalize, resize to 64³)
3. Used provided segmentations (HD-GLIO-AUTO / DeepBraTumIA)
4. Extracted tumor regions via connected components
5. Tracked regions across timepoints (IoU + centroid matching)
6. Extracted quantitative features (volume, growth, shape, spatial)
7. Classified progression (rule-based engine)
8. Demonstrated 3D U-Net architecture (implemented, can train on GPU)
9. Trained attention LSTM for temporal progression (CPU, ~5 min)
10. Ran ablation study (total vol vs region-wise vs full framework)
11. Demonstrated hidden regional changes invisible to total volume

**Models:**

- `R/03_model_3d_unet.R` — 3D U-Net (encoder-decoder, skip connections, Dice+CE loss)
- `R/08_model_lstm.R` — Attention LSTM (temporal sequence → RANO classification)

The 3D U-Net is architecturally verified on CPU; full training requires GPU (Colab/cloud).
The LSTM trains fully on CPU since it operates on extracted features, not raw images.
